title: RED tests carry a guaranteed-fail marker

facts.note: Only test files are subject to the RED gate. Any bun:test file (TypeScript or JavaScript) is in scope; the core TypeScript pattern set is the accepted marker vocabulary, not a language eligibility filter.

The declared `Phase: RED` header is read by the existing validator bun_tester_discipline_detector (source implementation), which scans RED-phase files. Files with no declared phase are skipped (phase-declared owns that finding). Applies to every RED-phase file scanned, not only changed ones.
Emitted by the existing validator bun_tester_discipline_detector; it is a whole-file result (the RED-phase file contains none of the accepted markers), not a per-case fact.

fires: A bun:test file declares `Phase: RED` and contains none of the accepted guaranteed-fail markers anywhere in the file.
A JavaScript bun:test file declares `Phase: RED` and contains none of the accepted markers (marker vocabulary is the core TypeScript set; the file language does not exempt it).

A bun:test file declares `Phase: RED`, its cases contain only behavioral assertions, and no accepted marker appears anywhere in the file (the per-test obligation still applies to each case, but the detector finding is file-level).
doesNotFire: A test file declaring `Phase: GREEN` or `Phase: REFACTOR`.
A test file with no declared phase (that is phase-declared's finding).
A RED case that has a marker but lacks a behavioral witness (that is red-behavioral-assertion's finding, not this marker detector's).
Flagging `it.fails` / `test.failing` as a self-skip (no-self-skip deliberately does not flag them).

given: A bun:test test declaring Phase: RED
when: the RED test is written, edited, or scanned by the RED gate
then: Each RED test MUST contain at least one accepted guaranteed-fail marker: `throw new Error('Not implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`, `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, `it.fails(`, or `test.failing(` (bun:test's spelling of `it.fails(`, accepted identically).
prefer: Write the behavioral oracle first (required by red-behavioral-assertion): derive it from the bound acceptance's Given/When/Then so it fails because the behavior is not implemented correctly.
Then add one marker after the stimulus runs, e.g. `expect.fail("<behavior> not implemented yet");` or `throw new Error("Not implemented: <behavior>");`.
Remove the marker in GREEN only once the behavioral assertion carries the proof and passes.
avoid: Using the marker as the only meaningful reason the test is red.
Throwing before the declared stimulus is exercised.
Wrapping a vacuous or already-passing case in `it.fails` / `test.failing`.
Weakening the behavioral assertion because the marker already guarantees failure.
why: Failing-first is a runtime property no static detector can observe; the marker is the decidable structural proxy. It aids the detector; it is not the RED objective or the behavioral oracle.
evidence: Detector finds at least one accepted marker in every `Phase: RED` file; reviewer confirms each RED case carries one.
The case also contains the behavioral witness required by red-behavioral-assertion.
Running the target case confirms it reaches the intended behavior.
Causal check: apart from the structural marker, the behavioral oracle would still fail for the expected missing-behavior reason without relying on the unconditional marker.
verifier_detail: File-level detector: flags any `Phase: RED` file containing none of the core TypeScript RED markers (transcribed from CORE `red.convention.yaml` -> `red_patterns.typescript`): `throw new Error('Not implemented …')`, `throw new UnimplementedError(…)`, `expect(false).toBe(true)`, `expect(true).toBe(false)`, `expect.fail(…)`, `return Promise.reject(…)`, `it.fails(` / `test.failing(`. The detector is exactly this structural proxy check; it does not report per-case absence when another case in the file supplies a marker. The pattern set defines the marker vocabulary; it does not restrict which bun:test files (TS or JS) are scanned.
`test.failing(` is bun:test's spelling of vitest's `it.fails(` and is accepted identically.
Files with no declared phase are skipped; that is `phase-declared`'s finding.
`it.fails` / `test.failing` are markers, NOT self-skips — `no-self-skip` deliberately does not flag them.
Term red_marker: a guaranteed-fail construct: throw new Error('Not implemented…'), expect.fail(…), expect(false).toBe(true), return Promise.reject(…), it.fails( / test.failing(.

Term structural_proxy: what this rule checks. Whether a test ACTUALLY fails first is a runtime property; core supplies the decidable stand-in. The obligation is agnostic; only the marker syntax is stack-specific.
Complementarity: `red-behavioral-assertion` asks whether the case encodes the missing behavior; this rule gives the static gate evidence that the artifact is intentionally in RED.

A test whose only meaningful reason for failing is `expect.fail(...)`, an unconditional throw before the stimulus, or a failing wrapper around an otherwise passing case is mechanically red while the acceptance remains unproven.
audit: Bun realization of core `tester.red.test-must-fail-first`, mirroring `tester.convex.red-fails-first` rule for rule.
Original fix_hint example markers: `expect.fail("checkout rejection not implemented yet");` // or `throw new Error("Not implemented: checkout rejection");`
Original fix_hint section headings: 'Behavioral proof:', 'Structural proxy:', 'Avoid:', 'Verify:'.
